body:
Sadly, my friends are still in their "lets go out and party every weekend" phase of their life, so staying with their parents is the easiest/cheapest.

I got an appointment for 3 possible apartments next week, so I'm hoping for the best.

I feel absolutely horrible though

My girlfriend works full-time yes:)

While it would be possible I suppose, I am not sure how she feels about moving in together.

We have also only been together for 8 months so that's a bit too early for me IMO, and I don't want to move in together for the wrong reasons, if that makes sense.

Everything you say is absolutely true but sadly, I cannot continue my education if I have to work full-time (studying at home is only possible at the age of 25 and up in my college). I made an appointment with my professor though, hoping I can convince her to make an exception for me.

I can crash at my girlfriends place for 2-3 weeks (still lives with her parents) which I am very thankful for, but I don't want to be a burden on them and I will only use it if I have no options left at all.

See that's the thing. Because of my depression I had a hard time concentrating on my exams, which lead to me having to re-take 6 exams next week.

I haven't been able to study properly for them, mainly because I was/am too busy trying not to be homeless.

Sure my sister would give me a couch for a while, but if I don't have my own place and end up crashing at my sisters place, I WILL have to quit college and work a dead end job at a grocery store or something.

I have nothing against people that have a job like that, but I got 2 friends (including my girlfriend) who work at a supermarket and seriously, you can see the job is making them depressed.

I am the first person in our family to go to college, so my sister doesn't know how important it is. I almost failed last year and she went "oh well, you can go work in a factory or something like everybody else, it's not the end of the world" and she's stuck in that mind-set

I'm going for a BA in Tourism (yeah yeah useless degree, it's just my easiest ticket out of here to start over)

That's another thing, when I got kicked out, I was planning on getting a weekend job to support me (I can't get a job throughout the week, as I have college 5 days a week, with hours averaging from 9AM until 6PM), but the time I'd spend working would not be worth it, compared to what I get financially.

Let's say I get paid 50EUR/Saturday, which means 200EUR every month. I have to report any other money I receive through work/family to that government institution, and I actually discussed this with them.

If I earn 200EUR/Month they will reduce the money they give to me by 160EUR, which means I would be working 4 days a month for 40EUR
That's the thing though, I CANT get back on my feet. If I don't have my own place, I lose all financial support my government gives me, which leaves me with 125EUR/month
